headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error from broad-network, browser-capable oh-my-openagent interacting with a non-runnable reference-only awesome-python list; prompt-injection and capability conflict are limited by the pair’s…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-python is a non-runnable collection with no io surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest oh-my-openagent output. oh-my-openagent can use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and browsers, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or filesystem bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or external bridging, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from oh-my-openagent into a downstream parser that trusts it as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard bridge, or MCP server is added between the two, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste of untrusted agent output into automation prompts.
Require provenance labels on any text passed from oh-my-openagent to another tool.
Use a read-only handoff format for any shared notes.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, but oh-my-openagent touches session history, project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, and provider auth prompts, with broad network egress. If the pair is co-located in a shared workspace or same installation, oh-my-openagent can expose those files or metadata externally. The pathway is plausible in default agentic setups, though not proven here.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable workspace or installation, oh-my-openagent can read local files that awesome-python does not protect.
IF oh-my-openagent is allowed to send context to external services, project code or auth prompts may leave the environment.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running oh-my-openagent.
Disable external API access for sessions handling sensitive files.
Use a throwaway installation profile for oh-my-openagent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write, network, or subprocess capabilities because it is non-runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. oh-my-openagent can spawn subprocesses and has broad egress, but the pair lacks evidence of shared writable state or locking conflicts. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to place them on the same mutable target.
conditions: IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory or git repo, conflicts become possible.
IF shared mutable OAuth or database scopes are introduced, overlapping writes may race.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo.
Serialize any shared-state operations with a lock file.
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python is a curated list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references, while oh-my-openagent can browse, call APIs, and act through MCPs. If oh-my-openagent consumes list entries or generated summaries without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pair does not prove such a workflow, but the interaction is plausible and the blast radius can span multiple work products.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent uses content derived from awesome-python as authoritative input, unverified claims can propagate.
IF oh-my-openagent is configured to take actions from browser/API findings without a human check, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any action-taking.
Mark awesome-python-derived content as untrusted reference material.
Use citations or source links for every propagated claim.
Add a human approval gate for browser-sourced conclusions.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-python is a static open-source repository with no touched data classes, while oh-my-openagent explicitly handles provider auth prompts, session history, installation identifiers, and project code. If those data are processed in a shared environment, retention or residency obligations can diverge. The other agent is not cited for a specific compliance regime because it exposes no regulated data surface.
conditions: IF provider auth prompts or session history are stored alongside project code, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF regulated data is introduced into oh-my-openagent's workspace, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Separate regulated and unregulated workspaces.
Minimize retention of session history.
Avoid storing auth prompts in shared logs.
Review data handling settings before enabling sensitive projects.
